file_note: First goals, written 2026-10-04 from today's facts. EVERY DATE AND OWNER SEAT IS PROVISIONAL until Zach approves them. A goal whose approval is null shows PROVISIONAL on the board and is counted apart from approved goals; approval names the owner decision file that approved the test and the date. The Greenfield sign-off gates arrive later as a second goals file with its own lock. This file is the goals of record: its authority is the protected branch of the goals-of-record repository (a rule changes only when a commit reviewed by Zach lands there). Locally it is also locked by hash (goals.lock) and by the newest LOCK-LOG.md entry; prepare a change with: check.py relock --od 00-owner/decisions/OD-....md, which lists every changed goal on the board in red for 7 days.

goals.title: The scoreboard checker is running (it reported in the last 30 minutes)
goals.done_means: The checker wrote its heartbeat file within the last 30 minutes. It is read at the start of each run, so it shows the PREVIOUS run: a gap of more than 30 minutes (a sleeping Mac, a stopped job) shows up here on the next run and stays in history.jsonl. The first run ever shows 'no heartbeat yet'.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner. A stale scoreboard is also visible in the feed (freshness), because a dead checker cannot report on itself.

goals.title: The Studio has at least 30 GB free disk
goals.done_means: The real data volume of the Studio reports 30 GB or more free (1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes, same as df -g). Free space inside the HLWork sparsebundle does not count; this reads the host disk. It measures the machine it runs on, so it can only be checked on the Studio (its Bonjour name is Mac-Studio): run on any other machine, such as the checker of record on Camp David, it is CANNOT CHECK (amber) and never a green or a red about the wrong machine.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner. The 30 GB line is the floor charter's Maintenance alarm. Standing rule: from the due date on, a failure is red. Until the checker of record can read the Studio's disk over ssh (needs HQ: a key for the checker account, then a relock with ssh_host), it reads CANNOT CHECK on that account.

goals.title: Camp David has at least 30 GB free disk
goals.done_means: A one-shot ssh to Camp David reports 30 GB or more free on its data volume. If ssh cannot connect, the goal is CANNOT CHECK (amber), never green.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner. Needs the ssh key to work from the job that runs the checker.

goals.title: The /login page shows the one sign-in's first screen
goals.done_means: The public /login page answers 200 within 10 seconds and shows the sign-in's opening line, 'And you are?'. That is only the first screen. It does not prove a visitor can sign in: goal T2-SIGNIN-END-TO-END is the real sign-in goal.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner seat. Green here means only that the first screen answers; it is not the sign-in being done. The real goal is T2-SIGNIN-END-TO-END.

goals.title: A test sign-up gets a texted code and lands as one lead in the CRM
goals.done_means: A test sign-up (name and email or Google, then the phone number, then the texted code) ends as exactly one lead in the CRM. This is the real sign-in goal. The check stays CANNOT CHECK, never green, until Lee enables it; it is the only check that is ever allowed to submit a form.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner seat. Not enabled yet: it reads CANNOT CHECK (amber) and turns red after the due date, so the sign-in cannot look done on the first screen alone (see T2-SIGNIN-LIVE).

goals.title: Forced registration is off on houseloop.ai
goals.done_means: The live registration-settings endpoint is read as JSON and its forced_registration.on value is exactly false (the JSON value false, not the text, not 0). Another switch in the answer being off does not count, a repeated key makes the answer unreadable (CANNOT CHECK), and text that merely looks like the switch inside another field does not count. Floor charter rule 9 and the retracted forced-registration ruling: no forced registration.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL date and owner seat; the test itself is approved by OD-20261004-SEO-MASTER-PLAN-AND-KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH (Zach retracted the forced-registration ruling). If Zach turns forced registration on, this goal must be relocked citing his decision.

goals.title: robots.txt on houseloop.ai is unchanged (nothing blocks crawlers)
goals.done_means: The live robots.txt is byte for byte the file Zach saw on 2026-10-04: 655 bytes, fingerprint a6cd3521... Any change turns this red the same day, whoever made it. This only reads the file; the checker never touches it.
goals.note: PROVISIONAL. Date is the day the standing rule (never block crawlers) was ordered, so a change is red at once. If Caleb's approved SEO plan changes robots.txt, relock with Zach's words.
